Hi Asha — thanks for the clear spreadsheet and timeline. High-level answers below and I've attached a short one-pager and links to the evidence pack in Drive. Karthik and Lauren are looped in for technical and contractual clarifications.

Executive summaries (2–3 lines each):
- Hosted API: Redwood-hosted, multi-tenant inference offering. We operate the control plane and serving runtime in our cloud tenants; customer data is encrypted in transit and at-rest per our standard KMS policies. Customers use API keys; no customer-managed network connections.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools provisioned for a single customer within Redwood-managed infrastructure. Logical isolation at runtime, dedicated tenancy for inference; customer workloads run on isolated pools with per-customer logging and retention settings. Data and model artifacts are segregated; keys may remain in Redwood-managed KMS or, with a contractual addendum, be integrated with customer KMS.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer-managed networking. Control plane can be run as a managed control plane with connectors into the customer's VPC, or fully on-prem for air-gapped deployments. Customer is responsible for underlying network, firewall rules, and physical access. Redwood provides deployment scripts, runbooks, and can integrate with customer HSM/KMS.

Responsibility matrix (short):
- Redwood: serving runtime, kernel/optimization updates, application-layer logging, runtime patches, model runtime security and CVEs, SLAs for uptime (Hosted/Dedicated)
- Customer: network isolation, identity providers, physical hosts (on-prem), backups of data stored only in customer-controlled storage (Private)

Differences callers should be aware of:
- Key management: Hosted/Dedicated default to Redwood KMS; Private supports customer KMS/HSM.
- Audit log access: Dedicated and Private can provide per-tenant logs and longer retention on request; Hosted has constrained retention due to multi-tenant data policy.
- Fallbacks: In Dedicated we provide automatic fallback to compatible instances within the customer's reserved capacity; Hosted users can be routed to model variants across regions as configured by routing policy.

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private) — technical detail

Asha / Marissa — quick technical follow-up to populate the SIG free-text fields. Pointing to specific controls and evidence files.

1) Encryption and keys
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS optional for Private connectors; Hosted and Dedicated use TLS with TLS termination at our ingress.
- At rest: All customer-derived artifacts are encrypted using AES-256. Hosted/Dedicated default to Redwood KMS with per-tenant encryption contexts. For Dedicated and Private, we support customer-provided KMS (via cross-account IAM roles for cloud KMS or HSM integration on-prem). Evidence: SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (attached) and KMS-integration-runbook in Drive.

2) KV cache & prefix caching
- KV cache lives in Redwood-managed memory for Hosted and Dedicated to accelerate repeat requests; cache is ephemeral and not stored to persistent storage in Hosted flow. For Dedicated, we can enable optional encrypted snapshotting to customer-provided object storage if required. For Private, KV cache deployment is controlled by the customer and adheres to their storage policies.

3) Audit logs & retention
- Hosted: 90-day standard retention for request/response metadata; token-level content logging restricted and redaction policy applies.
- Dedicated: default 1-year retention for access logs and per-token metadata retained for 180 days; can be extended under contract.
- Private: retention is customer-configurable; Redwood will support delivery pipelines to the customer's SIEM.

4) Network diagrams and firewall rules
- Attached network diagram illustrates NAT/egress patterns for Hosted vs. dedicated enriched with VPN/connectors for Private. For Private (VPC) we recommend dedicated subnets and strict egress rules; we will provide a hardened ruleset template.

Attachments: network-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.png (image), SOC2-summary-2026.pdf (pdf)

If Riverton needs a short techno-ops blurb for the SIG row (50–100 words) per deployment mode I can draft those and add them to the answers spreadsheet.
